ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo; Real Decreto 304/2014, de 5 de mayo, por el que se aprueba el Reglamento de la Ley 10/2010; Real Decreto 98/2018, de 2 de marzo, por el que se regula el Registro de Titularidades Reales; Orden JUS/319/2018, de 21 de marzo, por la que se aprueba el modelo de formulario de declaración de titularidad real.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport of ultimate beneficial owner and all subscribing shareholders
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Country-of-origin national police, consulate, or competent passport-issuing authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified translation (sworn translator) of proof of registered address and bank reference letter for each non-resident shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Originating bank and translating interpreter sworn before the Spanish Ministry of Foreign Affairs
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization (non-Hague Convention origin states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of each corporate shareholder or parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Originating commercial registry or Companies House

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, and UBOs against Spanish domestic PEP/EIP lists maintained by SEPBLAC, the National Intelligence Center, and the Penal Courts; against EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; UN Security Council Sanctions List; OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List; and Interpol/Red Notice checks. Enhanced due diligence is required for PEPs, high-risk jurisdictions, and any unusual commercial relationship inconsistent with a low-risk PropTech SaaS platform.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry) - https://www.rmc.es
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be expressed in Spanish or any EU official language transliterated into Latin script; the name must be lawful, not misleading, not identical or phonetically/semantically similar to an existing registered name, and must end with the entity type 'Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada' or its abbreviation 'S.L.'; all corporate documents and the deed must be in Spanish unless a sworn translation is attached.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may submit a new application for a negative name certificate with a different proposed name at the Registro Mercantil Central online portal or via a notary. If the rejection is based on material error or prior right, the applicant may file an administrative appeal within one month before the Dirección General de los Registros y del Notariado (DGRN) and, ultimately, judicial review before the contestable-administrativo chamber of the Audiencia Nacional. The name certificate, once granted, is non-extendable; if the incorporation deed is not executed within the 180-day validity period, a new certificate must be obtained.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible for registration purposes provided the address is physically located in Spain, is accessible for service of process, and is accepted by the notary and registry. However, for a SaaS/PropTech platform handling third-party rental payments, the Spanish Tax Agency (AEAT) and SEPBLAC may require a real operational presence or an appointed tax representative if revenue thresholds are met. Fully virtual structures without any fixed establishment are high-risk for permanent establishment classification and VAT registration purposes.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notarial fee scale regulated by Real Decreto 1426/1989, based on share capital and deed complexity

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sworn translation of foreign-language corporate documents and UBO declarations
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Sworn translator appointed by the Spanish Ministry of Foreign Affairs, European Union and Cooperation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark per document and page count

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Provisional NIF (Spanish tax identification number) application and handling

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Spanish corporate legal counsel retainer for pre-incorporation due diligence and drafting of bylaws (Estatutos Sociales)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for cross-border SaaS entity setup, typically fixed fee or hourly rate

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, por el que se aprueba el texto refundido de la Ley de Sociedades de Capital (Capital Companies Act), Articles 19-22 (incorporation formalities), 58-60 (registered office), 62-64 (minimum capital), 209-238 (board of directors)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry) for name certification; Registro Mercantil Provincial (Provincial Commercial Registry) for deed registration
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public deed of incorporation (escritura de constitución) granted before a Spanish notary and subsequently registered in the Mercantile Registry
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum paid-up share capital for an SL is €3,000 (approx. USD 3,250), fully subscribed and paid up in cash or in-kind at incorporation; capital must be deposited in a Spanish bank account formalized via a bank certificate (certificado de desembolso) and can only be released after registration
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscription and fully paid issuance of the share capital of the Company, as set forth in the deed of incorporation, be and are hereby ratified and accepted. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the Company be established at Calle de la Tecnología 12, Madrid, Spain, unless changed by subsequent resolution. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the individuals named in the instrument of incorporation be and are hereby appointed as Directors with the authority to act jointly or severally as the law permits. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the Company open bank accounts, execute all customary documents, and file all necessary registrations and tax forms to commence operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Foreigner Tax Identification Number (NIE) for all non-resident incorporators
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish Consulate in incorporator's country or national police station (Comisaría General de Extranjería y Fronteras) in Spain
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form EX-15, provide passport, proof of incorporation purpose, and pay administrative fee; if applying in Spain, submit at the immigration office with a valid visa; the NIE is assigned within 1-2 weeks.
required_dossiers: Form EX-15 (duly signed)
Valid passport and copy of all pages
Evidence of purpose (e.g., intention to incorporate a company)
Consular or immigration fee payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If application is queried or incomplete, submit amended form and additional supporting documentation; reapply with corrected details; engage a local gestor to expedite.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Negative Name Certificate from the Central Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry), Madrid
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File an online application for certification of no conflicting trade name (certificación negativa de denominación social). Submit up to three proposed company names; the registry verifies availability and issues a certificate valid for 3 months.
required_dossiers: Application form signed by all promoters
Copy of NIE and passport (or corporate power of attorney) of the applicant
List of proposed corporate names
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any proposed name is rejected, the registry will indicate the conflicting name; resubmit with the next available name on the list; pay a new fee only if the certificate is reissued.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open a Spanish Bank Account and Deposit Share Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank in Spain (e.g., Santander, BBVA, CaixaBank)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Select a bank and submit the name certificate, NIE, passport, and draft articles of association (estatutos). The bank will open a provisional company account and issue a bank certificate certifying deposit of the €3,000 minimum capital. This certificate must be included in the public deed.
required_dossiers: Negative name certificate
NIE and passport of all incorporators
Draft articles of association
Proof of commercial address (utility bill or lease)
Bank risk and AML forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank delays account opening due to enhanced due diligence on non-residents, provide additional source-of-funds documentation and a local reference; request a provisional identification from the bank; or use a bank familiar with cross-border tech companies.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute the Public Deed of Incorporation Before a Spanish Notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish Notary (Notaría) with jurisdiction over the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Schedule a notary appointment. All incorporators must appear in person or through a granted power of attorney. Present the name certificate, bank certificate, articles of association, and NIE numbers. Sign the deed (escritura de constitución), which must include bylaws, capital structure, registered office, and appointment of initial directors. The notary will handle the payment of corporate income tax (ITPAJD) on capital operations.
required_dossiers: Original negative name certificate
Bank certificate evidencing capital deposit
Passport and NIE of each incorporator (original and copies)
Power of attorney, if any incorporator is not present
Draft articles of association (estatutos)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary raises deficiencies in the deed or missing documents, correct the bylaws or provide supplemental certificates and reschedule; the deed can be re-executed with rectification without penalty if done before registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Apply for the Provisional Tax Identification Number (NIF provisional) and Pay Transfer Tax
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria, AEAT)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month after execution of the deed, submit Form 036 to the AEAT to obtain the provisional NIF (declaration of start of activity). Simultaneously, the notary must liquidate the Capital Transfer and Stamp Duty Tax (ITPAJD) on the capital increase via Form 600. After registration, the provisional NIF must be converted to definitive.
required_dossiers: Copy of the public deed (first copy)
Form 036 (duly signed)
Form 600 for ITPAJD
Power of attorney or authorization of the legal representative
NIE and passport of the representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the provisional NIF is not granted due to errors in Form 036, correct the form and resubmit; any ITPAJD deficiency will trigger a supplementary assessment with a 20% surcharge, so ensure timely filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the Company in the Provincial Mercantile Registry and Obtain Definitive NIF
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial (Provincial Commercial Registry) corresponding to the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the first copy of the public deed with the Provincial Mercantile Registry within two months after notarization. The registry verifies legal compliance and issues the registration certificate. After registration, present the registration certificate and provisional NIF to the AEAT to obtain the definitive NIF (Form 036 amendment).
required_dossiers: First copy of the public deed
Evidence of provisional NIF
Form 036 (cancellation of provisional NIF)
Stamp: registration fees (aranceles)
Certified copy of NIE and passport of the director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a calificación (objection) based on legal defects, apply for sub-sanation by amending the deed or articles; present an additional aclaración to the notary and re-file. If the deadline is missed, request a late filing with justification and pay applicable additional fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Formalities: Social Security Registration, Municipal Operating License, and Software/SaaS Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social (TGSS); Municipal City Council (Ayuntamiento); Secretaría de Estado de Digitalización e Inteligencia Artificial (SEDIA) for data and digital compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company as an employer with TGSS (Form TA.6) and register directors/managing employees for social security. Apply to the municipal council for an opening/activity license (licencia de apertura) for the registered office, which for a pure PropTech software company is subject to municipal urban planning and fire safety review. Implement GDPR compliance, e-invoicing, and software services registration if applicable.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the public deed and registration certificate
Definitive NIF certificate
Municipal license application form (declaración responsable or solicitud de licencia)
Fire safety certificate and electrical inspection for the premises
Employment contracts (if staff hired)
Data protection policy and privacy documentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipal license is refused or delayed, correct the building/security deficiencies and appeal the administrative denial within one month (recurso de alzada); for social security issues, submit missing documentation electronically at the TGSS electronic office.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Municipal City Council (Ayuntamiento) – Local Business Licensing Department (no sector-specific industrial authority for PropTech/SaaS)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licencia de Apertura (Municipal Opening License) or Declaración Responsable for offices without public access

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico (MITECO) – Environmental Impact Assessment Division; regional environmental authority if applicable
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – The activity is a knowledge-based software platform (ISIC 6201 / NAICS 531390) with no industrial installation, physical manufacturing, or significant environmental footprint; the EIA procedure is not triggered under the Ley 21/2013 de evaluación ambiental.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable (no wastewater, VOC, or hazardous waste generation from core operations). Office activities must comply with municipal waste separation and common industrial or commercial waste management standards (Law 7/2022 on circular economy) and, for office discharges, comply with municipal sewer discharge limits under the Consolidated Water Law.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate (certificado de protección contra incendios) issued by a competent technical officer and approved by the local fire department; structural load compliance certificate for the registered office; workplace health and safety assessment (evaluación de riesgos laborales) under the Ley 31/1995 de Prevención de Riesgos Laborales; and occupational clearance for use of IT equipment and electrical installations per the Low Voltage Electrotechnical Regulation (REBT).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT); official electronic portal: Sede Electrónica at https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es. Basque Country and Navarre have separate provincial tax authorities (Diputaciones Forales/Hacienda Tributaria de Navarra) for certain local taxes, but AEAT administers VAT, excise, customs and most corporate income tax.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL) must obtain a provisional NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) through a notary or the Mercantile Registry upon incorporation and file Form 036/037 with AEAT to register in the Census of Economic Activities; a definitive NIF is issued after filing. A foreign non-resident entity undertaking Spanish taxable activities must obtain a NIF de entidad no residente from AEAT by appointing a fiscal representative, submitting Forms 036/030 with certified constitutional documents, proof of existence, power of attorney and identification, and being assigned a NIF which for VAT purposes is used as the ES VAT identification number. For intra-EU operators, the Spanish VAT ID is ES + NIF.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; Territorial_Scope: worldwide taxation for Spanish resident SL; Pass_Through_Eligible: No (an SL is not fiscally transparent under Spanish general law); Tax_Exempt_Zone: Not generally available, except the Canary Islands ZEC (Zona Especial Canaria) for approved new companies carrying on qualifying activities and subject to a special reduced corporation tax rate.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain does not permit check-the-box classification. An SL is automatically a corporate taxpayer. Optional elections relevant to a real-estate PropTech SaaS holding entity include: (i) consolidated tax group regime for groups with 70% direct/indirect capital and control (elections are binding and require annual reporting); (ii) VAT group registration for closely linked resident entities for VAT aggregation; (iii) elections under the hybrid mismatch and ATAD implementation laws (e.g., reverse hybrid entity treatment and subject-to-tax exclusions); (iv) limited transparency for certain pension/regulated collective entities; and (v) for small new resident SLs, the 15% reduced Corporate Income Tax rate for the first two taxable years is mandatory rather than elective.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: IVA (Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido) - Spanish value added tax, derived from EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC; no state-level sales or use tax; plus excise/customs duties where applicable.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 0: VAT registration is mandatory for any entity carrying on taxable business activities in Spain, regardless of turnover level. There is no general small-business exemption. Non-established foreign suppliers registering under the One-Stop-Shop (OSS) in Spain trigger Spanish VAT obligations on cross-border distance sales of goods (intra-EU threshold EUR 35,000 per calendar year if not already registered) and on electronically supplied services to EU consumers; the importation of low-value consignments is subject to separate OSS/IOSS rules but does not exempt a principal VAT registration in Spain.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Spain requires e-invoicing in B2B relationships under 'Ley Crea y Crece' in the Facturae XML format (phased in from 2024/2025), and AEAT's 'VeriFactu' regulation (RD 1007/2023) requires certified billing software, a QR identifier, hash-link chaining and immediately extractable records for all invoice-oriented transactions. Large taxpayers with turnover over EUR 6,000,000 and VAT-group registrants must submit VAT entries almost in real time under the Suministro Inmediato de Información (SII) system (typically within 4 or 8 days). No general mandatory AEAT clearance stamping exists for ordinary SMEs, but the system permits AEAT real-time digital audit access to invoice data.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Physical exports of goods from Spain to a destination outside the EU qualify for 0% VAT exemption with refund entitlement under VAT Act Article 21 if the goods are transported out of the EU customs territory and the exporter retains proof of dispatch. For the PropTech/cloud SaaS service scope, offshore business-to-consumer digital services are outside Spanish VAT where the consumer is established outside the EU; B2B digital services to customers in other jurisdictions are outside the scope/reverse-charged if the customer is a taxable person in another country, and EU B2C digital services fall within OSS reporting. Services directly related to exported goods (e.g., logistics, loading/unloading) may also be zero-rated. Merely providing cloud software to a foreign real-estate client does not constitute export of goods and must be analysed under place-of-supply destination rules.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUA/electronic SIE or SOCIE clearance) referencing the Spanish VAT exporter's NIF and the 0% export key
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill signed by the carrier evidencing physical exit from the EU customs territory
Commercial invoice and packing list tied to the customs declaration
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank credit advice proving receipt of the export sale proceeds from the foreign purchaser in the required foreign currency
Proof of entry into the destination country, or any alternative evidence requested by AEAT under export proof rules
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT has a five-year limitation period and can reopen historical VAT filings if export proof documents are missing or false. Recharacterisation from an exempt export to a taxable domestic supply triggers immediate assessment of 21% VAT on the invoice value, late-payment interest, and a tax-prudence sanction of 50% to 150% of the underassessed VAT (increased for concealment, repeated conduct, or use of forged invoices/customs declarations). Export zero-rating may be clawed back across the whole bundle of transactions and fraud penalties are reinstated. Where amounts defrauded exceed EUR 120,000, criminal tax fraud under Spanish law carries imprisonment of 2 to 6 years, fines up to six times the defrauded amount, and loss of eligibility for public benefits and tax settlements; directors and responsible managers may incur personal and joint-and-several liability.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), operating within the Eurosystem and the European System of Central Banks (ESCB). Foreign-exchange and cross-border capital-movement supervision is shared with the Dirección General de Transacciones Internacionales of the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Business. Statistical reporting of external transactions is governed by Banco de España Circular 4/2012, as amended, and by the Registry of Foreign Investments (Registro de Inversiones Exteriores, RD 571/2023).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible; Spain applies complete current-account and capital-account liberalisation under TFEU Articles 63-66, with no prior authorisation required for profit remittance or capital repatriation. Dividend distribution to non-resident shareholders is permissible after satisfaction of the Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL) corporate tax obligations and application of the 19% non-resident dividend withholding benchmark (reduced under applicable double-tax treaties). Remaining frictions are procedural: (i) statistical declaration to Banco de España for individual cross-border transactions at or above EUR 1,250,000 and for payment-aggregation thresholds; (ii) EU/UN sanctions and asset-freeze screening under Regulation (EU) 833/2014; (iii) screening of non-EU foreign direct investment in regulated or critical-technology sectors - a PropTech SaaS platform under ISIC 6201 is generally outside the critical list, but a confirmation via the Registro de Inversiones Exteriores is recommended; (iv) Model 720 annual information filing for foreign bank accounts, securities and assets exceeding EUR 50,000 per asset class; (v) data-residency and GDPR constraints on real-estate screening data stored or routed outside the EEA.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain imposes no statutory surrender timeline and no mandatory conversion ratio for export or SaaS revenue receipts. The SL may hold export proceeds in EUR or foreign currency indefinitely. Compliance obligations are documentary and statistical: (i) receipts must be credited to a Spanish credit institution unless a direct declaration to Banco de España is made; (ii) supporting evidence must include DUA customs declarations, commercial invoices, proof-of-delivery and SWIFT MT103 confirmations; (iii) cash or cheque settlement between economic operators is restricted to EUR 1,000 under the anti-money-laundering regime of Law 7/2012, as amended; (iv) individual export payment transactions at or above EUR 12,500 may trigger bank-level statistical capture, and aggregated direct reporting to Banco de España is required at the EUR 1,250,000 threshold within the statutory filing window.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Multi-Currency Account (EUR/USD) with SWIFT corporate portal
Operational Account (cuenta operativa) with e-commerce clearing and TPV integration
Operational Account plus Escrow/Garanty Account (cuenta de garantía) for rental-screening deposits
Corporate IBAN Operational Account with digital onboarding and payroll direct debit
Technology/SaaS Operational Account with treasury-line and FX forward capabilities
Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account for regional commercial presence

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Rating: HIGH for ancillary treasury rails, MEDIUM as the sole banking relationship. EU-licensed electronic-money institutions (Wise Europe - BE; Revolut - LT; Airwallex - NL; MultiPass - FI) and Spanish EMIs (Unnax, Hito) may passport payment services into Spain under PSD2 and provide instant multicurrency IBANs, SWIFT/SEPA transfers, virtual cards and efficient EUR-USD-LATAM FX execution. Legal constraints: EMIs are not credit institutions; safeguarding balances are not covered by the Spanish Deposit Guarantee Fund (FGD); Agencia Tributaria (AEAT) and Social Security direct debits generally require a Spanish credit-institution IBAN; and EMIs cannot issue commercial documentary credit. Recommended treasury architecture: tier-1 Spanish bank for tax payments, payroll and credit facilities, supplemented by one EMI treasury rail for LATAM collection aggregation and contractor disbursements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is generally admissible for EU-resident directors and beneficial owners of a resident SL through accredited video-identification, subject to Banco de España AML guidelines; approval typically completes in two to six weeks. Non-EU or LATAM-resident directors and UBOs materially increase friction: most tier-1 banks require an in-branch interview of the legal representative and the apostilled original passports, NIE certifications, and a board resolution approving account opening. For capital escrow formation, the notary coordinates with the credit institution to issue the capital-deposit certificate (certificado de desembolso); this may be completed remotely if the participants already hold accounts with the same bank. A physical presence in Madrid or Barcelona is not legally mandated but materially accelerates senior-risk sign-off for treasury limits and FX lines.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: LATAM non-resident shareholders and complex intermediate holding chains creating opacity in the Registro de Titularidades Reales (beneficial-ownership register).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Extract from the Registro de Titularidades Reales; notarised certificate of incorporation and deed of appointment of directors; tax-residency certificates of all UBOs; source-of-funds file (audited financial statements, bank statements, sale and investment contracts); chain-of-title maps for invested capital; PEP screening sign-off; sworn declaration of beneficial ownership.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PropTech SaaS platform processing rental-screening and property-management data with high-volume subscription inflows from third-party merchant accounts (Stripe Billing) that may resemble unlicensed payment intermediation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master SaaS subscription agreement and landlord/property-manager mandate letters; evidence that the SL never takes possession, custody or settlement of tenant rental funds; Stripe account ownership certificate and reconciliation reports; PCI-DSS Level 1 attestation; DPIA and GDPR compliance register; client due-diligence records on commercial landlords; annual AML risk self-assessment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound equity injection with round-number amounts, rapid subsequent disbursement, or funds from jurisdictions with high AML index scores.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised capital-increase deed; bank certificate of disbursement (certificado bancario de desembolso); Banco de España statistical declaration for external transactions using the foreign-direct-investment code if the threshold is met; investor KYC (passport, proof of address, corporate registry extract); source-of-wealth statements and tax returns of the investors; intercompany loan agreement and transfer-pricing documentation if booked as debt.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expectation of tax-optimisation movements, treasury round-tripping, or mismatch between business profile and payment-charge descriptors on SWIFT messages.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Group cash-pooling and treasury policy; monthly reconciliation between Stripe settlement reports, bank statements and invoicing records; VAT (IVA) and corporate tax (IS) filing history; sanctions screening logs of vendors; evidence of economic substance (employees, leased office, software IP ownership) and audit trail of all treasury entries.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant injection route: (i) EU-source funds transferred by SEPA Credit Transfer, non-EU funds via SWIFT MT103 quoting the relevant Banco de España transaction code (3001 foreign direct investment in capital, 4001 shareholder loan) in field 70; (ii) funds credited to the EUR-denominated operational account held with a Spanish credit institution; (iii) ex-ante filing of the Banco de España external-transactions statistical declaration follows for individual transactions at or above EUR 1,250,000, with the month-end aggregation declared via the corresponding T1/T2 electronic returns; (iv) for non-EU investors, screening status is confirmed through the Registro de Inversiones Exteriores; (v) source-of-funds verification requires investor KYC, apostilled board resolutions of the investing entity, and an updated shareholding chart; (vi) the funds are then capitalised by public deed before the Commercial Registry or booked as a shareholder loan under a Spanish-law veri pact.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Disbursement rails for an estimated EUR 40,000 monthly vendor outflow: (i) SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) for EU suppliers with T+1 clearing; (ii) SEPA Instant (SCT Inst) for urgent payroll and tax-critical payments; (iii) SWIFT MT103 for non-EU contractors in LATAM and Asia, with explicit purpose codes and retention of the cover message for proof of payment; (iv) documentary Commercial Letter of Credit (sight LC) for hardware, cloud-infrastructure and data-centre procurement above EUR 100,000, against invoice and transport documents; (v) Stripe Issuing virtual cards with per-vendor limits for cloud subscriptions (AWS, Azure, Datadog); (vi) US ACH Direct overlay via the EMI rail for low-value USD-denominated SaaS reseller payments. All non-EUR payables are settled from treasury sweep balances in the USD subaccount under an internal FX-hedge policy to avoid unmanaged currency exposure.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD deliverable FX forwards (up to 12-month tenor) with Santander, BBVA, CaixaBank or Bankinter treasury counterparts under ISDA 2002 Master Agreement, executed on a bilateral non-cleared basis as a non-financial counterparty (NFC-).
Non-deliverable FX forwards (NDFs) in EUR/CLP, EUR/BRL, EUR/MXN and EUR/ARS for LATAM receivables where the underlying currency is non-deliverable onshore or subject to local capital controls.
Cross-currency basis swaps (EUR/USD and EUR/LATAM-USD) for long-term shareholder loans above EUR 1,000,000, with EMIR clearing-threshold assessment documented in the treasury policy.
Outright buy-side European-style FX options (EUR call / USD put and EUR call / MXN put) acquired exclusively as premium-paying protection; writing of options is outside the permitted hedging mandate.
FX swaps (spot versus forward) executed with the clearing bank under the same master agreement for the rolling conversion of USD subaccount balances into EUR operating liquidity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of Annual Accounts (Depósito de Cuentas Anuales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local Registro Mercantil (Commercial Registry) in the province of the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after shareholder approval; approval must occur within six months from December 31 fiscal year-end, i.e., no later than July 31 of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Economic penalty up to EUR 2,000 plus 'cierre registral' (loss of registry validity for subsequent filings) if filed late or not filed; repeated non-filing for three years may trigger statutory file closure and loss of benefits.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return (Impuesto de Sociedades, Form 200)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 days following the six-month period after the tax year end; for calendar-year taxpayers, by July 25 of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment surcharges (5% to 20%) plus statutory interest; late-filing penalties from EUR 200 to 2% of turnover; possible asset seizure for unpaid tax.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Between January 1 and January 30 following the calendar year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing fines of EUR 200 to EUR 2,000 or 2% of VAT due; VAT assessment with surcharge and interest on errors.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Together with Form 200: by July 25 for calendar-year taxpayers, only if aggregate transactions with a given related party exceed EUR 100,000.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine of EUR 300 to EUR 20,000 per missing or inaccurate item, depending on the corrective statement; may be assessed together with corporate tax penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Register of Final Beneficial Owners (Registro de Titularidad Real) – event-driven update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil local (coordinated with the beneficial-owner platform managed by the Ministry of Justice and AML authorities)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No annual confirmation cycle; any change in ultimate beneficial ownership must be reported within 10 days of the acknowledged change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing of UBO changes may incur registry refusal and sanctions up to EUR 180,000 under anti-money-laundering law in serious cases.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit if two of three thresholds are met in two consecutive financial years: total assets exceed EUR 4,000,000; net turnover exceeds EUR 8,000,000; average headcount exceeds 50 employees.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Plan General de Contabilidad (Spanish GAAP, PGC) for individual accounts; IFRS-EU applicable to consolidated financial statements when required.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Spain does not impose a standalone annual UBO declaration. The existing legal registry obligation is event-driven: UBO changes must be registered within 10 days. Annual accounts filings implicitly include current shareholding and directors but do not re-confirm UBO separately.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro Registro de Socios)
Register of Directors (Libro Registro de Consejeros)
Inventory and Annual Accounts Ledger (Libro de Inventarios y Cuentas Anuales)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying 'empresa emergente' status under Ley 28/2022 grants a reduced 15% CIT rate for the first taxable year with a positive tax base and the following three tax periods, subject to AEAT certification. The capitalisation reserve (art. 25 LIS) reduces the taxable base by up to 10% of the annual increase in equity retained, provided the funds are maintained for 5 years. R&D and innovation tax credits under art. 35 LIS reach 25% of eligible software and SaaS development expenditure and 42% of certified R&D spending; a 20% credit applies to patented software/IP exploitation and may be monetised by low-turnover innovators. Loss carryforward is indefinite under art. 26 LIS (field value '0' denotes unlimited carryforward); offset is capped at 70% of positive taxable base where prior-year net turnover exceeds EUR 20 million and at 50% where turnover exceeds EUR 60 million, while sub-EUR 20 million SMEs may offset 100%.
